extracted.intended_audience: general readers and travelers interested in Japanese culture and customs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive standards for composing or evaluating travel/observational writing about Japan (etiquette, scenes, institutions, and practical travel rules as portrayed in a late‑19th/early‑20th century travel narrative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Imperial audience ceremony protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Ceremony at the Imperial Diet: the reading 'not more than three minutes'; Prince Tokugawa went up from the floor to the platform, received the scroll from the Emperor’s hand, returned to the floor, made a final bow; the Emperor descended from the throne and exited; 'All were enjoined to remain in their places until the Emperor had left the House; the audience then dispersed without further regard to order or to precedence.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises brevity, formal sequence of steps, deference while the Emperor is present, and that the dispersal was informal only after the Emperor's exit. Presented as an example of a simple but impressive public ritual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threats to parliamentary/constitutional government
rubrics_metrics.description: Distrust of government arises because 'the legislators seem so largely under the control of the struggle... between the now privileged classes... and the socially lower... in their efforts to wrest away these advantages.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one fault most threatening to Japan's parliamentary cause is 'a certain inability... to avoid the evils of an extreme partisanship and to learn that art of practical compromises'. Use this as a criterion when evaluating success or stability of constitutional government: degree of partisanship and capacity for compromise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpersonal approach with Japanese (etiquette for foreigners)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Japanese 'do not gratefully tolerate being looked down upon, or even condescended to... They respect... the person who deals with them in manly frankness, and on terms of manly equality' and 'admire and practice... the proper mixture of quietness and politeness in manner with courage and firmness at the heart (suaviter in modo, fortiter in re).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interacting with Japanese of the period, avoid condescension, treat people as equals, be frank but polite; combine quiet politeness of manner with inner firmness. This is presented as the preferred behavioral standard for foreigners seeking respectful relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military leadership demeanor ('du calme')
rubrics_metrics.description: For a great field-marshal or general the essential quality is 'Du calme' — keep the cool head and the unperturbed heart with a steady pulse-beat; private soldiers may show excitement but not the officer in command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an evaluative characteristic of competent command: calmness and composure under strain distinguish effective leaders from undisciplined troops. Cited from General Ian Hamilton's account of Japanese military opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and practicalities for travel in Japan
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel impressions depend heavily on weather; custom of early rising and early breakfasts; absence of sleeping-cars historically; travellers should guard against summer sun with pith hat and umbrella but cannot readily defend spirits against prolonged rain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice for travellers and travel writing: note the dependence of scenic experience on weather, anticipate early schedules, and account for historical transport limitations when describing journeys. Use practical local preparations (hats, umbrellas) as concrete travel details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passport and travel legal requirements (historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tourists visiting places beyond ten ri (~24.5 miles) from a treaty-port 'must obtain passports from the Japanese Government by application through the diplomatic representative' and state purpose ('for scientific information' or 'for the benefit of the health'), exact route, and length of time; applications for more than three months likely refused. Inn/tea-house keepers were required to take up the passport and hand it to local police for inspection and safekeeping until the guest's departure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing or planning travel in historical Japan, include these formal passport constraints and their local enforcement; they affected itineraries and lodging. The text offers an anecdotal example of strict compliance differing by locality and instances where locals tried to accommodate strangers despite the law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe boat design for rapids (Katsura‑gawa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boats considered safest and most manageable: 'very broad for its length, low, and light; with its bottom only slightly curved, fore and aft, and toward both sides.' The boards between passengers and the water were thin so one could feel them bend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these boat design elements as criteria when evaluating or describing craft used on whitewater: breadth, low profile, lightness, slightly curved bottom. Also mention seating on blankets and presence of multiple boatmen for control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boatmen skill and management as safety criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Experienced boatmen—four to a craft with roles (steersman, two oarsmen, one with a pole)—had piloted thousands of persons down the Katsura-gawa 'at all stages of its waters, with a loss of only five lives' over fifteen years; skilful management reduced trip time under favourable conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging safety and reliability of river excursions, emphasise crew experience, division of labor, and past safety record (casualty statistics). Anecdotes about disputes among boatmen or occasional strikes on rocks offer realistic context for assessing risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenic elements that create aesthetic charm
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenic charm derived from combined features: excellent roads, durable stone bridges, continuous gardens and frequent villages, multitude of jinrikishas and carts, terraces covered with verdure and flowers, bamboo groves producing delicate chiaroscuro, clumps of azaleas, waterfalls, and maple groves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For travel description or evaluation of landscape beauty, point to these concrete, repeatable elements (infrastructure, vegetation, light/shadow effects) and use sensory language (e.g., 'chiaroscuro') to convey the visual effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives and methods of Japanese public education
rubrics_metrics.description: Public education places pupils under 'a close-fitting system of physical and intellectual drill' calling out pride and ambition; uses 'Imperial rescripts, the wise sayings and noble achievements of ancient sages and heroes, the arousement of that spirit called 'Bushidō' or 'Yamato‑Damashii,' [and] instruction in ethics... prolonged from the kindergarten to the University' with the intention 'of producing citizens serviceable to the State.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating the school system's aims, assess extent of moral/ethical instruction, use of national/rescript materials, emphasis on drill and discipline, and the explicit state orientation toward producing obedient, serviceable citizens. Note both strengths (order, politeness) and acknowledged weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct standards in military per the Imperial Rescript
rubrics_metrics.description: Imperial Rescript: 'Soldiers must be polite in their behaviour and ways... The junior must obey the senior... Superiors must never be haughty and proud toward those of lower rank, and severity of discipline must be reserved for exceptional cases. In all other cases superiors must treat those beneath them with kindness and especial clemency.' If courtesy is lost, one 'will be... committing serious crimes against the country.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Rescript's provisions as explicit normative criteria for military and hierarchical behaviour: politeness, obedience, moderation in discipline, humane leadership. Cite this as an institutionalized standard, not merely social expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Etiquette for visiting schools and public ceremonies
rubrics_metrics.description: Visitors should accept local requests: make short talks (ten minutes), allow interpretation, participate in ceremonial acts (e.g., planting commemorative trees), let pupils have the chance to see off guests (boys preceding to river bank and shouting 'banzai'), and compromise on requests with courtesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing or conducting visits to schools, follow local protocols: speak briefly, coordinate with hosts for interpretation, partake in symbolic acts, and show reciprocal respect. These actions are presented as both expected and effective in generating goodwill.
